The black boxes for the town this is in can be resolved to a place I lived for a while and am familiar with, so I found myself trying to figure out where in town the house is… and coming up with a plausible answer that explains a local oddity makes it all the better.

Except for the part about the cover story being a "ranch". The Northeastern US isn't real big on ranches, and I can't think of anywhere in the area where a "ranch" could plausibly be used as a cover story.

A house where everything is a conceptual load-bearing item. I like it, and I feel like there's some interesting story potential in it. +1

This is similar to something I wrote a few years after the fact. As far as I know, I didn't read this before writing my own article, but it's cool to see how an underlying concept (a dwelling where moving stuff changes other stuff) diverged into very different ideas.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: One small detail bothers me. How do you have roughly 3294 items? 3294 is an exact number. It would make sense to have exactly 3294 items or roughly 3290 items, but roughly 3294 doesn't make a whole lot of sense. I'd say exactly 3294, as that would mean that containment officers might be able to tell if one is missing. If they only have an approximate number, it's unclear if one is missing.

item.title: An explanation?
item.content:encoded: Ok here's an idea for what's going on. And entity is on another plane but in the general proximity of the house and it's trying to get people to collect these artifacts and arrange them so it can come to our plane. But when we started to mess with the artifacts, things started to screw up, and it started getting frustrated. And it REALLY got pissed when the foundation removed the artifacts it needed. That's why the earth started to heat up. And when they returned the artifacts, it calmed down.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This article is being placed up for review. Check it out, this one needs some more attention.

So, the containment procedures seem a bit excessive. If the things in the house are only active if you arrange them in a certain way, why the hell do we have a nuclear warhead underneath the site? That seems hella over the top. The Sears Catalog Home thing seemed a bit silly, as well as the Feng Shui. It could just have the object arrangement without all the obscure references. I really do like the idea of objects in a home making a whole bunch of supernatural shit going on depending on the arrangement, but it's totally killed by the expungement in the addenda. It totally takes the interesting elements out of this, and really deflates the overall effect the piece had on me.
